decisions.question: Does the intended NTFS checkpoint target satisfy the bounded CEML-CKPT-1 durability contract
decisions.selection: supported: generation-directory store with FlushFileBuffers on both files and on the directories, same-directory MoveFileExW write-through publication, content-based recovery
decisions.decision_rule: R4 section 14 and I1 section 13: documented semantics plus bounded forced-termination tests
decisions.rationale: All 78 interruption scenarios and all 13 adversarial cases passed with fresh-process recovery and continuation, for both serialization strategies, with every R4 section 14.5 phase forced. No partial or inexact generation was ever published or accepted; the previous validated generation was always retained; the pointer was never trusted; corrupt newest generations, chain breaks and foreign identities were refused. Safety does not depend on rename durability: a generation is retired only after its successor was flushed, published, directory-flushed and re-read, so a lost publication falls back to a generation whose files were already flushed.
limitations: Process interruption only; no power-loss proof
Volatile device write caches that ignore flush requests are outside this evidence
Rename atomicity under power loss is not stated by the retrieved documentation
Bounded CEML-CAL-1 engineering evidence on this machine and build only; not V1 and not a scientific-scale forecast

Same backend and compiler with a larger language surface

decisions.selection: C17 with the documented public GMP mpz interface, pinned Microsoft C toolchain
decisions.rationale: Only the C17 family has a complete pinned, offline-reproducible local dependency closure. C++20 would use the same compiler and the same C interface and adds no capability; Rust with rug has no offline dependency closure here. Tie-break: smaller surface, fewer dependencies.
limitations: Bounded CEML-CAL-1 engineering evidence on this machine and build only; not V1 and not a scientific-scale forecast

decisions.question: Local resource ceilings for bounded calibration
candidates_considered: revised ceilings with bounded admission wait
decisions.rationale: Isolated one-second page-input excursions occur with no CEML arithmetic and with zero page output, so one excursion cannot indicate case-caused memory pressure. Two consecutive excursions or any page output still refuse or abort. Admission waits a bounded, recorded time with no work in progress. All refusals are retained.
limitations: Page input is a non-specific proxy; temperature is unavailable; the processor-performance floor is a frequency-collapse stop only
Bounded CEML-CAL-1 engineering evidence on this machine and build only; not V1 and not a scientific-scale forecast
